newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela to road-show Banco Consolidado.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela to road-show Banco Consolidado.

text.p: Venezuela is to road-show sate- owned bank Banco Consolidado in Europe ahead of a hoped-for sale in the fourth quarter of this year, bank President Luis Hinestrosa said.
"We've been invited to give presentations in France and Spain", Hinestrosa told a news conference, adding that so far five European and Latin American banks had shown interest.
The bank is slated for a late 1996 sale, alongside Banco de Venezuela whose first privatisation attempt earlier this month flopped amid legal uncertainties.
Consolidado was taken over by the state in September 1994 and has since shown an "extraordinary improvement" in its financial health, Hinestrosa said.

Deposits have grown to 311 billion bolivars from 92 billion, the number of clients has grown from 300,000 to 1.1 million, and its loan portfolio has risen to 89 billion from 13 billion at the beginning of 1995.
